CHAPTER 2 — WHAT ABOUT SEX? SBD’s answer is not prudishness, nor permissiveness. It is clarity. Sexuality, in its originative design, is not shameful; it is sacred. But sacred things mishandled bring harm. CHAPTER 3 — HOW AM I A PART OF IT? BIRTHRIGHT AND DESIGN 3.1 THE BIRTHRIGHT OF SEXUAL DESIGN Every man and woman is born into the inheritance of sexuality. It is not something added later in life; it is intrinsic to our very creation. Genesis 1:27 says: “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.”  Genesis 2:25 And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed. These verses establishe that our very identity is sexual in design: male and female. T o be male or female is not a cul-tural assignment; it is a divine biological birthright. Herein lies the question: “How am I a part of it?” The answer: because by your anatomy and being alive, you are already “part and parcel” of the sexual design. Sexuality is not a choice or an optional accessory to humanity — it is humanity itself, the protology of humankind. 3.2 STEW ARDSHIP OF DESIGN If sexuality is birthright, then literacy is stewardship. CHAPTER 5 — SEX = MARRIAGE:  THE ONLY EQUATION THAT WORKS5.0 INTRODUCTION The world often presents sex and marriage as two diﬀerent realities: sex as a biological or recreational act, marriage as a social or legal contract. But the SBD philosophy insists: sex is marriage by divine design, and marriage is con-summated and sustained by sex. Anything less fragments God’s blueprint for oneness. As Jesus pointed back to Genesis, and Paul echoed in Corinthians, the union of man and woman is not deﬁned by paper but by the one-flesh covenant enacted through sexual fidelity. Oneness is not imagined, symbolic, or bu-reaucratic—it is conjugal, physical, and spiritual. 5.1 BIBLICAL ANCHORS OF THE ONE-FLESH REALITY “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.” — Genesis 2:24 (KJV) This ﬁrst declaration deﬁnes marriage as sexual and covenantal. No certiﬁcate existed in Eden; no magistrate presided. What established oneness was the divine design of sexual union—man and wife cleaving into one ﬂesh. “What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.” — 1 Corinthians 6:16 (KJV) Paul’s comparison reinforces the same reality: even in sinful misuse, sex creates a one-body bond. If union with a prostitute establishes one-ﬂesh, how much more the covenant union of husband and wife! “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.”
